title: How GLM built its own inference infrastructure
why_read: A detailed writeup of how a Chinese lab built custom LLM inference infrastructure offers rare concrete engineering insight into serving large models at scale.
analysis: This piece describes how the team behind the GLM model family engineered their own inference stack rather than relying purely on off-the-shelf serving frameworks. Such writeups are valuable because production LLM inference involves subtle tradeoffs in batching, KV-cache management, quantization, and hardware utilization that are rarely documented outside a few large labs. The large comment count suggests engineers are engaging with specific technical claims, likely comparing it to vLLM, SGLang, or TensorRT-LLM approaches. This is exactly the kind of systems-engineering detail that is hard to find and genuinely useful for practitioners building or evaluating inference infrastructure.
